fig1_eigen_ellipse.svg: Eigenvectors as the axes of an ellipse. A symmetric $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&0.8\\0.8&1.4\end{bmatrix}$ maps the unit circle (dashed) to an ellipse (solid); its principal semi-axes lie along the orthonormal eigenvectors $v_1,v_2$ with lengths equal to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\approx0.85,\ \lambda_2\approx2.55$ (from `eig_symmetric`), since $A v_i=\lambda_i v_i$.
fig2_jacobi_convergence.svg: How `eig_symmetric` works: cyclic Jacobi rotations drive the off-diagonal Frobenius norm of $S=\mathrm{tridiag}(1,2,1)$ to zero. The decay is super-linear (note the log scale), reaching machine precision within a few sweeps; the converged diagonal reproduces the exact eigenvalues $2,\,2\pm\sqrt2$, matching the module's `eig_symmetric`.
